description: We're two NYU-CUSP graduate students looking to study the surface of the NYC metro area using the SAR data given to visualize how the city is slowly sinking. The plan is to create an interactive dashboard that highlights critical infrastructure in NYC that is sinking.
summary: We created a web explorer that measures how the tides in Jamaica Bay's marshes change using NASA's NISAR radar. Used 51 NISAR acquisitions over Jamaica Bay's marshes with radar backscatter to analyze the tidal changes in the region from 7 November 2025 to 21 October 2026. We wanted to develop a metric to see if more specular reflection off the water surface can be used to understand marsh habitat loss in the region and to validate the restoration efforts going on.
details: Used 51 NISAR acquisitions over Jamaica Bay's marshes with radar backscatter to analyze the tidal changes in the region from 7 November 2025 to 21 October 2026. We wanted to develop a metric to see if more specular reflection off the water surface can be used to understand marsh habitat loss in the region and to validate the restoration efforts going on. We created a public GitHub repository that contains the web explorer, the cloudflare workers storing the R2 data, and a docker backend to support the pulling of the NISAR data. We used Python scripts to obtain, validate, and analyze the data. Created a REACT/Vite app to showcase the images from the NISAR data and made a scrollable content to view the change of the marshes over time. The functionality of the frontend was created in Typescript with some basic CSS to design the page.
